title: GA4/GTM basics: what to measure to make optimization meaningful
excerpt: Without measurement you optimize by gut feeling. Track at least enquiries, CTA clicks, forms and the traffic sources that bring qualified leads.
description: Without measurement you optimize by gut feeling. Track at least enquiries, CTA clicks, forms and the traffic sources that bring qualified leads.
coverAlt: GA4 and GTM event and conversion tracking
segments: Many businesses say they have analytics, but all they really track is page views. That is a visit counter, not useful analytics. If you fail to measure what matters to the business, campaigns learn from the wrong signals and decisions rely on misleading numbers. Then everyone wonders why Meta spends too much or Google seems expensive, without knowing which channel produces actual, qualified enquiries.

GA4 and GTM are not there to create pretty dashboards. Their job is to answer one question: where do enquiries come from, and why? Without that, you optimize by instinct, which can be costly in marketing.
Why 'we have analytics' often means very little

A common scenario in Montenegro is GA4 installed without a single meaningful conversion. Form submissions are not tracked. Calls, WhatsApp clicks and Instagram DMs are not tracked. You cannot identify which campaigns produced enquiries, where the landing page creates friction or where people abandon the process. Decisions are then made using CTR and CPC, which are secondary metrics.

Another scenario is incorrectly configured conversions: button clicks count as successful enquiries, page views count as results or events fire twice. Analytics shows 200 leads while the inbox has just 20 messages.
The minimum setup you need
This covers most real scenarios for local services and events. With these events, optimization can be meaningful.
1) Conversion: lead submission

For a website form, a confirmed submission is the primary conversion, not merely a click on the submit button. Ideally, trigger the event on the thank-you page or after a successful response so false clicks are excluded.
2) CTA clicks

Track contact, enquiry and call clicks. These are not final results, but show whether visitors attempt to contact you. If CTA clicks exist but submissions do not, the form or next step may be the obstacle.
3) Outbound clicks
If you use WhatsApp, Viber, mailto, telephone, Instagram DM or external booking links, track their clicks as outbound events. For many local businesses, these are major contact channels.
4) Scroll and engagement

These indicate where visitors stop. If everyone leaves around 25% scroll depth, the top section may be underperforming. If visitors leave before the FAQ, the offer may need proof or clarification. You need a few meaningful signals, not twenty engagement events.
5) Sources that bring quality

GA4 should show the source, medium and campaign associated with conversions, not just sessions. Without that, you cannot compare Meta and Google performance or identify which campaigns actually drive enquiries.
How to verify that tracking really works
One simple test saves considerable trouble:

Submit a test enquiry as an ordinary visitor. Immediately check whether the event appears in GA4 Realtime. Verify the source/medium for that test and compare the number of tracked enquiries with real inbox or DM submissions for the same period.

If GA4 reports 30 enquiries but you have received 10 messages, something is wrong. Events may be duplicated, clicks may count as submissions or page refreshes may trigger extra conversions. Until that is fixed, all optimization decisions rely on bad data.
What to optimize once measurement works
Once tracking is reliable, optimization becomes more controlled because you stop guessing.

You can compare which channels bring qualified leads, and more importantly, which campaign types generate genuine intent. You can see which creatives produce enquiries versus clicks only. You can identify website friction, such as abandonment before the CTA, forms that reduce conversions or poor mobile page speed.
Common mistakes

Treating page views as success. Tracking no conversions. Duplicate events inflating figures. Using the wrong conversion trigger, such as click instead of successful submission. Inconsistent UTM parameters that prevent campaigns from being attributed correctly.
When you measure the right conversion, you stop guessing and start optimizing.
FAQ
Do I need GTM if I have GA4?
GTM makes event tracking and maintenance easier. GA4 alone may not cover precise custom events, especially outbound clicks and complex form submissions.
What event should I configure first?

Track successful lead submissions if forms are the primary contact route. If calls or DMs are primary, track those link clicks. Your first conversion should represent the action that matters to your business.
